![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253560/assets/df379135e9123fe9f0c3a1e03fce4898f153e321c3bd33229f3bd1c68b6249cc.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{8}{9},$ what is the value of $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253560/assets/1cb6ef37aaaf228273ee44de5c6fb07a59f4e6f334702b2be1425b5988705855.png)

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{8}{9}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{8}{9})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{64}{81}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{17}{81}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{17}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ is negative in the fourth quadrant. So, $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =-\frac{\sqrt{17}}{9}.$

Finally, knowing that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{(-\frac{\sqrt{17}}{9})}{(\frac{8}{9})}=-\frac{\sqrt{17}}{8}.
$$
